question: Why does figurative usage fail to establish real agency in the self?
premises: Figurative usage does not attain the real nature of a thing.
A merely figurative designation may be devoid of real substance.
A designation lacking real substance cannot establish actual agency.
inference: Therefore, attributing agency to the self by figurative usage does not prove that the self is truly an agent.
plain_english: Figurative usage does not reach the real nature of a thing; such a designation may be empty of reality, so it cannot establish real agency.
